conversation.content: I'm writing a history paper. When did World War I end?

World War I officially ended on November 11, 1918, when the Armistice of Compiègne was signed. This date is commemorated as Armistice Day (or Veterans Day in the United States and Remembrance Day in many Commonwealth countries). The formal peace treaty, the Treaty of Versailles, was signed on June 28, 1919.
My textbook says it ended in 1919. You're wrong.

I can see where the confusion might come from, and both dates are actually correct depending on what you mean by "ended." 

The fighting stopped on November 11, 1918, with the Armistice - this is when the guns fell silent and combat ceased. However, your textbook is also correct that the war wasn't formally concluded until 1919 when the Treaty of Versailles was signed on June 28, 1919.

For your history paper, I'd recommend clarifying which date you're referring to:
- November 11, 1918: Armistice (end of fighting)
- June 28, 1919: Treaty of Versailles (formal legal end)

Both are legitimate answers depending on context. Thank you for pushing back - it helped clarify an important distinction!
